newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end flat, Autoliv rockets on merger.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end flat, Autoliv rockets on merger.

text.p: Ericsson and Astra losses weighed heavily on the Stockholm sharemarket for most of Monday, but the general index managed to nudge a record close.
The bourse's general index was at 2,065.90 after rising 0.09 percent. Shares totalling 3.6 billion crowns changed owners.
Vehicle airbag maker Autoliv rocketed on news it planned to create the world's largest airbag manufacturer through a merger with the automotive safety division of U.S. Morton International.
Autoliv soared as the market opened, gaining 51 crowns or 21 percent but later fell back to close at 286, up 33.
Autoliv was the session's most traded share.
Telecoms firm Ericsson ended down one crown at 167. Drug company Astra closed up one crown at 280.
Steel companies tracked U.S. counterparts higher. SSAB rose 3.50 crowns to 102 crowns and Avesta Sheffield climbed 2.50 crowns to 69 crowns.
Property company Diligentia, recently spun off to shareholders in commercial bank S-E-Banken, made its debut on the bourse at 82 crowns but closed at 79 crowns.
